title: Blend + Fallthrough Deployment Playbook for Low-latency Retail POC
summary: Working playbook capturing a hybrid deployment approach that blends Hosted API, Dedicated pool, and Private deployment patterns with an edge-oriented fallthrough path for a retail customer POC. Focus: preserve 95th-percentile latency <= 120ms for interactive shopper flows while minimizing cost and preserving data controls.
background: Customer: mid-market ecommerce platform with conversational product discovery and cart-assist flows. Primary constraints: sub-200ms p95 interactive latency target on product-search queries, PII in customer prompts for logged-in users, and wish to start on Hosted for speed but maintain an upgrade path to Private for compliance. They have seasonal peaks (~3x) and need graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
objectives: 1) Define routing and capacity split across Hosted / Dedicated / Private for POC. 2) Produce concrete configuration knobs (batching, cache TTLs, quantization) to meet latency and cost targets. 3) Create a fallback/fallthrough strategy to avoid request failures during spikes. 4) List test plan and gating for next-phase Dedicated or Private migration.
customer_context:
- 20M monthly active sessions; POC scoped to 5% traffic (bot-filtered).
- Two primary request classes: product-question (short prompts, strong latency sensitivity) and guided-dialog (multi-turn, higher tolerance).
- Data classification: logged-in user chat includes PII -> must be routed to compartments with KMS.
- Compliance timeline: proof-of-concept then possible Private pilot in 3–6 months.
constraints:
- Hard latency SLO for product-question: p95 <= 120ms.
- Cost objective: POC target blended cost <= $0.003 per query on average.
- Operational: limited infra ops on customer side for POC (no on-prem hardware).
- Security: PII requests must not traverse third-party buckets without encryption/KMS and audit logs.
deployment_options: Option A — Hosted-first with Dedicated burst: All traffic goes to Hosted API; configure Dedicated reserved pool as a regional burst for sustained high concurrency. Use simple routing by latency and cost tiers. Pros: fastest onboarding, minimal ops. Cons: Hosted has data residency limits, and cost can spike without strict rate controls.

Option B — Segment-by-data-class (recommended POC): Send anonymized public intents to Hosted; PII-containing and enterprise-authenticated requests route to Dedicated sandbox (customer-provisioned VPC peering optional). Private pathway reserved for later migration. Pros: isolates sensitive data, keeps onboarding fast for public traffic. Cons: more complex routing policy and identity checks.

Option C — Edge-fallthrough first: Deploy an edge microservice (lightweight inference cache + reranking) colocated with customer CDN. Edge handles simple scoring and prefix cache; miss -> fall through to Hosted or Dedicated depending on token classification. Pros: best p95 for simple queries, reduces origin load. Cons: additional engineering to maintain prefix caches and model variants at edge.

Option D — Private pilot for all logged-in traffic: Onboard Private (VPC) for entire POC, leave anonymous endpoints on Hosted. Pros: maximum control and auditability; Cons: longest lead time and adds infra ops.

Option E — Adaptive routing by cost and load: Smart router inspects request meta (latency sensitivity tag, token budget, user tier) and routes to the cheapest compatible model that satisfies p95 SLO. Pros: cost-optimized in steady state; Cons: develops complexity in testing and fallback behavior.
recommendation: For this retail POC we recommend Option B combined with an Edge-fallthrough pattern (Option C) for product-question flows: route anonymized short queries to Hosted for fast onboarding; route logged-in/PII requests to a Dedicated sandbox (encrypted, KMS-enabled). Deploy a small edge cache layer for the top 200 intents/queries to reduce p95 tail and absorb spikes. This hybrid reduces onboarding friction, maintains compliance for PII, and gives predictable performance for the most latency-sensitive paths.
recommended_config_snippets: Routing policy: if request.authenticated && contains_sensitive_flag -> route to dedicated://retail-sandbox; else if intent in edge-cache -> serve-from-edge; else -> hosted://latest-curated-model

Dedicated pool sizing (POC window): reserve 2 x A100-equivalent slots for steady-state 5% traffic (peak concurrency headroom 3x), autoscale +1 slot at 70% GPU utilization, scale down after 10m of sub-40% utilization.

Batching: product-question endpoints use max_batch_size=8 and max_wait_ms=6; guided-dialog endpoints use max_batch_size=16 and max_wait_ms=18 to increase throughput without violating p95 for long-turn flows.
Cache: prefix KV cache on edge with TTL=60s for product-question fingerprints, LRU size=50k keys; cache warm during launch using crawl of top search logs.
Quantization profile: use 4-bit quantization on Dedicated for guided-dialog model variants and 8-bit for Hosted curated model to balance quality and cost.
KMS/audit: Dedicated sandbox must enforce customer KMS key for logged-in flows and stream audit logs to customer-approved S3 with 30-day retention for POC.
Fallbacks: router fallback order: edge -> dedicated -> hosted; if all fail, return 503 with degrade mode (short canned response + async retry token).
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0: config + infra bake (Hosted routing rules, Dedicated sandbox reservation, edge cache prototype). 2) Week 1: internal soak with synthetic traffic and chaos tests (simulate 3x peak). 3) Week 2: invited beta (5% of user traffic) — monitor latency, error rate, token cost. 4) Week 3: expand to 20% if p95 and error targets met; otherwise iterate. 5) End of POC: present metrics and recommend Private pilot if compliance gating requires it.
test_plan_and_metrics: Primary metrics: p95 latency (ms), p50 latency (ms), error rate (% 5xx and timeouts), cost per query (USD), successful decrypt/keys usage count, cache hit rate
SLO gates for expansion: p95 <= 120ms, overall errors < 0.5%, cache hit >= 40% for product-question, blended cost <= $0.003/query
Load tests: steady-state at 5% traffic, spike test at 3x for 30min, spike-and-failover tests with Hosted capacity limited to force Dedicated usage.
Quality checks: monthly eval prompt set comparing Hosted vs Dedicated outputs for top 50 intents; track hallucination rate and average generation length.
workshop-notes: Attendees: Priya (SE), Evan (Solutions Eng), Marina (Infra), Liam (Customer Success), Sofia (Product). Key takeaways: customer prioritizes latency over small quality delta; security team will require an audit trail for PII within 2 weeks; CDN/edge partner is open to hosting a small cache VM. Questions left open: who owns edge cache runtime? can we re-use customer's existing KMS? what are cost approvals for Dedicated reservation?
decisions: Adopt hybrid routing: anonymized -> Hosted, PII -> Dedicated sandbox.
Implement edge prefix cache for top intents with initial TTL=60s.
Reserve 2 A100-equivalent slots for Dedicated sandbox during POC with autoscale guardrails.
